detailed_findings.finding: The proof only uses condition (i), thereby establishing a stronger nonexistence result than the lemma states.
The key liminf steps are valid: alpha>S implies an eventual lower bound g(n) >= n^S, and liminf = alpha implies infinitely many indices with g(N) <= N^(alpha+epsilon).

reason: The argument is mathematically coherent and complete. It proves a stronger statement than required: for r>1/4 there is no strictly increasing g:N→N satisfying (i) alone, hence a fortiori none satisfying both (i) and (ii). The two liminf-based claims are justified, the iteration and summation arguments are sound, and the final contradiction from r alpha^2 - alpha + 1 <= 0 with r>1/4 is valid.
